chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abu Usamah, who said:
I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so he brought closer to me a banana, and I ate it.
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet's companion eat when visiting Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This brief narration from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Imam’s approachable nature and the cultural context of food sharing in 8th-century Medina, where bananas were a valued delicacy. It serves as a foundational text in Shia jurisprudence for establishing the permissibility of bananas (*mawz*) and underscores the social etiquette (*adab*) of accepting gifts and food from the Imams as a sign of respect and spiritual connection.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abu Asma who said,
‘I went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> forwarded a banana closer to me, so I ate it’.
en.sarwar: 2. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from abu ‘Usamah who has said the following:
“I once visited abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. He brought banana nearer to me and I ate.’”
